procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - penile ulcer
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Painless sore on the penile shaft first noticed about 3 weeks ago, same size since. No discharge from it or from the urethra. No fever, rash, headache, vision or hearing change. Over the last ~6 months has had condomless sex with several partners. Last RPR nonreactive in October.
History: syphilis 2019 (treated; RPR nonreactive by 2021), gonorrhea 2019, chlamydial epididymitis 2020, HIV since 2022 - suppressed on ART, last ID visit 8/2025.
Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 1 tab daily.
Allergies: PENICILLIN - anaphylaxis in this office 2/2019 (needed epinephrine and the ED). Has tolerated ceftriaxone twice since.

O: Afebrile, vitals as charted.
GU: solitary firm, indurated ulcer on the shaft, painless to touch, clean base. Bilateral inguinal nodes enlarged, rubbery, mobile, non-tender, not fluctuant. No urethral discharge. Testes normal.
Skin: no rash on trunk, palms or soles. Mouth clear. Neuro: normal.

A: Indurated painless ulcer with rubbery inguinal adenopathy in a man with prior syphilis and new exposures - primary syphilis, reinfection, most likely.

P:
- RPR with titer today (prior titer nonreactive, so any reactive titer means new infection), urine GC/CT. Treponemal test not useful - positive since 2019.
- Treatment: penicillin is out given anaphylaxis. For primary syphilis, doxycycline 100 mg twice daily x 14 days is the accepted alternative, with close titer follow-up; desensitization is the other route and we can revisit if the titer doesn't fall. Will start once the RPR is back this afternoon.
- No sex until the sore is healed and treatment done; partners in the last 3 months need testing/treatment.
- Letter to ID.

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily for 14 days with a full glass of water; stay upright 30 minutes

orders.order: Notify ID of syphilis reinfection and treatment
orders.reason: primary syphilis in patient with HIV

documents.title: RPR result and treatment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
RPR reactive 1:64 (was nonreactive 10/2025). New primary syphilis.
Called pt. Doxycycline 100 mg BID x 14 days sent to his pharmacy - take with water and food, upright after, sun protection. Start tonight. Follow-up visit in about 2 weeks to look at the ulcer. Then RPR at 3, 6, 9 and 12 months. DPH report and partner notification - RN will call tomorrow.

documents.title: STI follow-up call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Spoke with pt. Took first two doses of doxy, no upset stomach. He is notifying two partners from the last few months himself and also agreed to DPH partner services. Syphilis case report faxed to DPH. Visit note and RPR faxed to ID clinic per PCP. Urine GC/CT pending.
Addendum 15:20: GC/CT not detected; pt informed via portal.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - syphilis follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Finished the 14 days of doxycycline on 2/9, every dose, no side effects. The sore shrank within a week and is gone. Groin lumps smaller. No rash, headache or vision change. Has not been sexually active since the visit.
Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide daily (ID). Allergies: penicillin - anaphylaxis.

Exam: vitals as charted. Penile shaft: ulcer healed, faint pink macule at the site. Inguinal nodes now small, soft, non-tender. Skin clear including palms and soles. Neuro normal.

A/P:
1. Primary syphilis (reinfection), treated with doxycycline 14 days - clinical response good. RPR at 3 and 6 months (orders in, standing), then 9 and 12. Expect a fourfold drop by 6-12 months; if it doesn't come, revisit penicillin desensitization with ID.
2. HIV - cleaned up the problem list: "acute HIV infection" from 2022 updated to HIV disease; on ART, suppressed per ID. ID aware of this episode.
3. Prevention: condoms; screening every 3 months while partners change. He'll book a visit for the fall.

Continue ART. Return 6 months.

documents.body: Hi Miles - your RPR is 1:16, down from 1:64 in January. That's a fourfold drop already at 3 months, which is a good sign the doxycycline worked. Next check at the end of July (order is in, walk in any morning).
